title: Metered Fallback Credits & Security-Q Response SLAs for Private Appliances
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: Enterprise customers requesting Private/VPC or on-prem packages often ask for two tradeoffs that are hard to reconcile: (1) a small baseline license fee that keeps procurement friction low, and (2) guarantees that production will not be impacted when on-prem capacity saturates. Current offerings either force large reserved commitments (Dedicated-like) or leave customers to handle outage mitigation themselves. Separately, sales/legal frequently hit multi-week delays responding to security questionnaires (SQs) which blocks procurement for regulated customers.

Objectives:
- Create a trialable packaging experiment that combines a modest base license + metered fallback credits for hosted execution, so customers get continuity while avoiding large long-term commitments.
- Define support tiers and emergency patch credits that map to customer risk profiles and upgrade cadences.
- Define a Security Questionnaire (SQ) intake and response SLA framework that reduces procurement latency and is trackable in SLAs.

Hypothesis:
If we offer a Starter On-Prem bundle with a small non-refundable license + a predictable bucket of metered fallback credits (hours or token-equivalents) and a clear SQ SLA, more mid-market customers will close without requiring full reserved capacity commitments, and total ARR from on-prem deals will increase while support costs remain bounded.

Proposed packaging (experiment design):
1) Starter On-Prem Bundle (target: mid-market / ISVs):
   - One-time license fee: $15k base for first year (covers first NODE and basic setup).
   - Included metered fallback credits: 500 inference-hours on Redwood hosted per month (consumable when on-prem pool is saturated). Credits billed overage at $0.12 per inference-hour.
   - Support tier: Standard (24x5 email, 24h initial response for Sev2, 72h for SQ intake).
   - Upgrade cadence: Optional quarterly minor updates; major version upgrades scheduled at customer opt-in windows (quarterly major with opt-in).

2) Enterprise Resilience Add-on (optional):
   - Monthly subscription: $2k/month to attach a 2,000 inference-hour monthly fallback pool shared across customer org.
   - Emergency patch credits: 8 credits included (each credit covers a guaranteed hotfix within 24h). Additional credits $400/credit. Credits roll month-to-month with a 3-month cap.
   - Support tier: Premium (24x7 phone + 2h initial response for Sev1).

3) Large-Scale Reserved Path is unchanged (for customers who want Dedicated-style committed capacity).

Security Questionnaire SLAs (new operational play):
- Intake acknowledgement: 48 hours.
- Standard SQ (<=40 questions, vendor-ready templates): 7 business days for initial completed response.
- Complex SQ (>40 questions or requires architecture diagrams/access): 14 business days with a staged delivery (answers + architecture + remediation plan).
- Fast-track: For Enterprise Resilience Add-on customers, 48-72 hours initial delivery for high-priority SQs (legal-approved).
- Deliverables: PDF response bundle, network diagram, RDOC link to confluence page, named SME contact.

Operational notes and instrumentation:
- Metrics to track for pilot: conversion rate (proposal->signed), time-to-sign, average annual contract value (ACV), number of fallback events per customer-month, total hosted fallback consumption, revenue from fallback overage, support ticket volume attributable to fallback events, SQ turnaround time.
- Dashboards: private-packaging/pilot in Console analytics. Add breakout panels for fallback consumption by org, monthly emergency patch credits used, and SQ turnaround histograms.

KPIs / Success criteria (30-day pilot):
- 15% lift in mid-market on-prem closes vs baseline cohort.
- Median SQ turnaround <= 7 calendar days for standard questionnaires.
- Fallback consumption average <= 20% of included credits across pilot customers (indicates sizing is appropriate).
- Support cost delta per customer <= $2k/year after emergency patch credits amortized.

Risks & mitigations:
- High fallback usage increases hosting costs: cap per-org monthly overage and throttle policy; require finance sign-off on overage price. Monitor 1:1 with pilot customers.
- Legal/Procurement objections to non-refundable base fee: offer creditable fees into first-year subscription for larger deals.
- Security team bandwidth for fast-track SQs: assign named SME pool and rotate on-call for SQ responses.

Dependencies: ["ENG-19177", "SEC-004-SQ-OPS", "LEGAL-082-contract-clauses"]

Rollout plan / timeline:
- Week 0-2 (Nov 2025): finalize pricing bands, legal language, produce Confluence PRD and playbook.
- Week 3-6 (Dec 2025): engineering telemetry hooks + billing events instrumentation (fallback consumption meter + credit ledger).
- Week 7-10 (Jan 2026): sales enablement, price sheet, SQ fast-track SOP, pilot signups (3-6 customers).
- Week 11-14 (Feb 2026): pilot execution, daily tracking, iterate on credit sizes.
- Week 15 (Mar 2026): evaluate metrics, decision gate (scale / iterate / cancel).

Deliverables:
- Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Metered+Fallback+Credits+Pilot
- Billing spec & events: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/1842
- SQ response playbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cSQPlaybook

Stakeholders: Sales (Enterprise), Legal, Security, Billing Engineering, Runtime Team, Customer Success.

Open questions:
- Should metered fallback credits be billed in inference-hours or token-equivalents? (Engineering preference: inference-hours for simplicity).
- Should credits be monthly-until-year or front-loaded for first 90 days to reduce early churn?
- What guardrails should trigger an automated sales handoff if fallback usage exceeds 50% for two consecutive months?

Next steps (owner: Miguel Santos):
1) Lock legal-approved contract language for non-refundable license and emergency patch credits (due 2025-11-12).
2) ENG to scope telemetry changes and estimate billing implementation (due 2025-11-20).
3) Security to staff SME roster for SQ fast-track (due 2025-11-18).
4) Identify 3 pilot customers and create one-pagers for sales (due 2025-11-25).
comments: 2025-11-06 - Kickoff: PM + Legal + Security sync. Legal flagged multi-jurisdiction tax considerations for non-refundable fees (action: finance to model).

2025-11-10 - Eng scoping meeting: billing requires a new meter type 'fallback_inference_hours' and a credit ledger; estimated 3 sprints. Runtime needs ability to mark requests as 'fallback' in router. ENG suggested using token-equivalent pilot for first 30 days for faster metric parity.

2025-11-12 - Legal update: approved contract phrasing for one-time license if customer signs an MSA addendum; requires a short exhibit for emergency patch credits. Assigned to LEG-072 for final review.
2025-11-15 - Security comment: agreed to staff two SMEs and one backup for fast-track. SME rotation proposal being drafted. Need to record response templates in Confluence.

2025-12-03 - Finance: modeled baseline with 10 pilot customers; projected fallback overage loss <= 4% of pilot ARR if average usage < 30% of included credits. Recommended $0.12/hour as conservative starting point.
2026-01-22 - Pilot kickoff: signed letters-of-intent from 3 customers (stealth names). Initial telemetry shows 60% consumption of included credits in org-STEALTH-1 (needs sizing review).
2026-02-10 - PM note: iterated on credit sizes; moved to 750 inference-hours for org-STEALTH-1 to reduce immediate overages. Legal requests a clause describing credit rollover cap (3 months).

2026-02-25 - Engineering: billing PR opened https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/1842 . Runtime PR for marking fallback requests opened https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2761
2026-03-01 - PM assessment: SQ median turnaround for pilot customers is 6 calendar days (meets goal). Next gate review scheduled 2026-03-15 to recommend scale decision.
release_notes: Pilot created: Starter On-Prem bundle + metered fallback credits; SQ SLA playbook; telemetry for fallback consumption. Target decision gate Mar 15 2026.
notes_for_sales: Use the one-pager template in Confluence. Emphasize reduced procurement friction (low base fee) and continuity via fallback credits. For enterprise customers who require zero-hosted fallback, route to Reserved Capacity offering.
